summary: MarSim is a map and spacewalk (EVA) planner for astronauts on Mars. It uses NASA data for three areas: the Bagnold dunes and boxwork formations in Gale Crater, and Jezero Crater. It calculates a safe route using an oxygen consumption map, with a maximum slope and oxygen reserve. During an EVA, the simulation monitors the crew’s oxygen levels and recalculates the route when obstacles are reported. It also includes a 3D view and a helmet view, and works in both Polish and English on desktop and mobile.
details: MarSim is an EVA planner for astronauts on Mars, built on NASA data for Gale and Jezero craters. It plans the safest walking route by oxygen cost, avoiding steep slopes, sand and boulders, and keeps a 20% oxygen reserve. During the EVA it tracks each astronaut’s oxygen and the margin for the walk back, and recalculates the route when hazards are reported. You can also walk the route in 3D from a helmet view. We built it with Python (FastAPI) and JavaScript (three.js), with data from HiRISE, CTX, THEMIS, MOLA and CRISM. The goal is safer, data-driven decisions on future Mars missions.
